The quantum binomial coefficient $\binom{h}{k}_{q}$ is naturally viewed as a sum over size- $k$ subsets of $[h]$ of monomial terms, i.e, $\binom{h}{k}_{q}=q^{c}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}J\subseteq[h]//|J|=k\end{subarray}}q^{2\sum_{j\in J}j}$ for some constant $c=c(h,k)$ . Given a size- $k$ subset $J\subseteq[h]$ , let $\binom{[h]}{J}_{q}$ denote the exponent of the monomial corresponding to $J$ in $\binom{h}{k}_{q}$ .

#### Definition 7.7.

The quantum weight $w_{q}(S_{1},S_{2})$ of a compatible pair $(S_{1},S_{2})$ on $\mathcal{P}(m,m)$ can be determined recursively as follows:

As a base case, we set $w_{q}(\mathcal{P}_{1},\emptyset)=0$ .

Let $U=\mathcal{P}_{1}\cut\sh(S_{2})=\{\eta_{i_{1}},\dots,\eta_{i_{h}}\}$ be the set of horizontal edges that are not in the shadow of $S_{2}$ , where $i_{1}<\cdots<i_{h}$ . Then $U\cut S_{1}=\{\eta_{i_{j}}:j\in J\}$ for some $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,h\}$ . We then set

$$ w_{q}(S_{1},S_{2})=w_{q}(S_{1}^{\prime},S_{2}^{\prime})+\binom{[h]}{J}_{q^{4}}\,, $$

where $(S_{1}^{\prime},S_{2}^{\prime})=\theta(S_{1},S_{2})$ .

Note that, if $(S_{1}^{\prime},S_{2}^{\prime})=\theta(S_{1},S_{2})$ , then $|S_{1}^{\prime}|\geq\min(m,|S_{1}|+1)$ and $|S_{2}^{\prime}|\leq\max(0,|S_{2}|-1)$ . Thus, any compatible pair is sent to $(\mathcal{P}_{1},\emptyset)$ under finitely many applications of $\theta$ , so 7.7 is well-defined.

Using the quantum weighting, we can construct a map from compatible pairs to broken lines that respects quantum weights. Let $(S_{1}^{(i)},S_{2}^{(i)})=\underbrace{\theta\circ\cdots\circ\theta}_{i}(S_{1},S_{2})$ .

#### Definition 7.8.

Let $\varphi:\CP(m,m,a,b)\to\BL_{-}(m,m,a,b)$ be the map taking the compatible pair $(S_{1},S_{2})$ to the broken line that bending at the wall $\mathfrak{d}_{(\ell-1)/\ell}$ with multiplicity $h+|S_{2}^{(\ell+1)}|-2|S_{2}^{(\ell)}|-|S_{1}^{(\ell)}|$ .

#### Theorem 7.9.

If $2b\leq m$ , the map $\varphi:\CP(m,m,a,b)\to\BL_{-}(m,m,a,b)$ is a $q$ -weighted bijection.

#### Proof.

The size of the set $J$ in applying 7.7 to the compatible pair $(S_{1}^{(\ell)},S_{2}^{(\ell)})$ is precisely $h+|S_{2}^{(\ell+1)}|-2|S_{2}^{(\ell)}|-|S_{1}^{(\ell)}|$ . Thus, the binomial coefficient factor that a broken line attains by bending at the wall $\mathfrak{d}_{(\ell-1)/\ell}$ is the same as the binomial coefficient in 7.7 attained by applying $\theta$ to the set of corresponding compatible pairs. ∎

Note that the positive angular momentum case is symmetric to the negative angular momentum case by reflecting the scattering diagram along the line $y=x$ . As a result of the bijectivity of $\varphi$ , we obtain an expansion formula in terms of compatible pairs for the quantum theta basis element $\theta_{(m,m),q}$ .

#### Theorem 7.10.

The theta basis element $\vartheta_{Q,(m,m)}$ in $\mathcal{A}_{q}(2,2)$ is given by

$$ \vartheta_{Q,(m,m)}=\sum_{(S_{1},S_{2})}q^{w_{q}(S_{1},S_{2})}X_{1}^{-m+r|S_{2}|}X_{2}^{-m+r|S_{1}|}\,, $$

where the sum ranges over all compatible pairs on $\mathcal{P}(m,m)$ .

#### Proof.

By definition, the theta function $\vartheta_{Q,(m,m)}$ can be expressed as a sum over broken lines. Using 7.9, the expansion formula in terms of compatible pairs follows directly by applying the bijection $\varphi$ to the corresponding broken lines. ∎

### 7.3. Equivalence of bases for the quantum Kronecker cluster algebra

Lastly, we show that, for the quantum Kronecker cluster algebra, the quantum theta basis coincides with a number of other bases. The bases we consider are

- (1) the quantum bracelets basis [30, Definition 4.9],

- (2) the quantum theta basis [9, Proposition 3.1]*,

- (3) the basis $\mathcal{B}$ consisting of the quantum cluster monomials and $\{z_{n}\}_{n\geq 1}$ in [10, Definition 3.4],

- (4) the quantum triangular basis [3, Theorem 1.4], and

- (5) the quantum greedy basis [18, Theorem 9].

The following discussion concerns only the quantum Kronecker cluster algebra, though these bases may coincide in a more general setting. All bases mentioned contain the cluster monomials, so it is enough to show that the remaining elements coincide.

The fact that (1) and (2) coincide is due to the recent work of Mandel and Qin [25, Theorem 1.4], who showed that the theta and bracelets bases coincide in a much more general setting.

To show that (2) and (3) coincide, it is enough to check that (the specialization of) $\vartheta_{Q,(1,-1,0,0)}$ and $z_{1}$ are equal. This is because the $z_{n}$ ’s satisfy the Chebyshev recursion of the first kind by definition, while Mandel and Qin [25, Example 5.8] showed that the same recursion holds for the theta functions $\vartheta_{Q,(n,-n,0,0)}$ . By comparing [6, Lemma 3.3] and [25, Lemma 8.4], it is readily seen that $z_{1}=\vartheta_{Q,(1,-1,0,0)}|_{y_{1}=y_{2}=1}$ .

The bases (3) and (4) can be shown to coincide by recent work of Li [23, Theorem 1.2] which determine the support of triangular basis elements for skew-symmetric rank- $2$ quantum cluster algebras. It is then straightforward to check that the supports of the elements $z_{n}$ are equal to the supports of the non-cluster-monomial elements in the triangular basis, so the bases coincide.

We can then show that (3) and (5) coincide by directly verifying that the elements $z_{n}$ satisfy the recursion given in [18, Theorem 7], which characterizes the greedy basis. We do so using the Laurent expansion of $z_{n}$ given by the work of Ding-Xu. It follows directly from [10, Proposition 4.4] that $z_{n}=s_{n}-s_{n-2}$ , where $s_{n}$ is the element

$$ s_{n}=\sum_{p+r\leq n}\binom{n-r}{p}_{q}\binom{n-p}{r}_{q}q^{-(2p-n)(2r-n)}X_{1}^{2p-n}X_{2}^{2r-n}\,. $$

This is a special case of the $q$ -analogue of the following lemma, which can be easily proved by the standard generating function method.

#### Lemma 7.12.

For any nonnegative integers $n,p,r$ with $p\geq r$ , we have

$$ \sum_{k=0}^{p}(-1)^{k}\binom{n-1-r}{p-k}P(k)\binom{n-2r+k-1}{k}=0, $$

where $P(x)$ is any polynomial in $x$ of degree $\leq r-1$ .

#### Remark 7.13.

We note that the basis consisting of the cluster monomials and $\{s_{n}\}_{n\geq 1}$ that appears in the work of Çanakçı and Lampe [6, Definition 4.15]* is not identical to these other bases. It instead coincides (after specializing and possibly reordering the principal coefficients) with the basis $\mathcal{S}$ from the work of Ding-Xu [10, Definition 3.4]. The elements $s_{n}$ are related to the elements $z_{n}$ in the basis $\mathcal{B}$ , and their Laurent expansion is given in Equation 7.11. The work of Çanakçı and Lampe was later generalized to quantum cluster algebras from unpunctured orbifolds by Min Huang [16].
